name: Mia Sloan
life: “I still remember a magazine holiday family with nobody washing dishes.” Sunday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Mia keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: The holiday photograph on my fridge is of somebody else's holiday. I want one ordinary breakfast picture of my own.
appearance: Mia is easy to recognize by short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak and heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a small enamel bird on the lapel, Mia folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing when listening.
personality: Mia prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To take one unposed breakfast photograph on holiday.
family: Alan Ko is Mia’s cousin. Mia calls about good news first. Alan is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The split visit*, Alan says, “I am the son who books the visits from overseas.”
connections: Ravi Foster. A holiday photograph doesn't need a sponsor's name across the front.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Mia asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.
